en: Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga Sekhiyakaṇḍa (The Section on the Training Rules)
2. The Second Training Rule on the Circular.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks put on their upper robes hanging them down both in front and behind... [as before] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall put on the upper robe evenly all around.
It should be put on evenly all around, having made both corners level."
If, out of disrespect, one wears [the robe] hanging down either in front or behind, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is lacking mindfulness, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
The second training rule is finished.
